page: Amazon Web Services r8a.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, providing a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores, falls within the average range. Memory performance is strong, with a Passmark memory score in the top 25% and DDR5 memory speeds of 6 GHz. The instance also demonstrates top-tier efficiency in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, alongside strong static web serving throughput of 53.16 GB/sec.

The instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8:1, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. Tradeoffs include the complete reliance on network-attached storage and the lack of hardware accelerators. This profile is suitable for memory-intensive applications such as database operations, caching layers, and small-scale language model inference.
